The physics simulation will be performed with the full level of detail, but the rendered mesh may be shown at a reduced level of detail.  Godot will automatically generate LODs when importing meshes, and its default settings will merge adjacent faces that are nearly flat in relation to each other.  This is desirable for static meshes, but often not what you want for soft bodies, if you want these faces to be able to bend and deform.  You may want to disable LOD generation or tweak the generation settings when importing meshes that you plan to use with [SoftBody3D].

```suggestion
		[b]Note:[/b] [SoftBody3D] will honor [url=$DOCS_URL/tutorials/3d/mesh_lod.html#doc-mesh-lod]mesh LODs[/url] when rendering the mesh. The physics simulation will be performed with the full level of detail, but the rendered mesh may be shown at a reduced level of detail. By default, Godot automatically generates LODs when importing meshes, and its default settings will merge adjacent faces that are nearly flat in relation to each other. This is desirable for static meshes, but often not what you want for soft bodies, if you want these faces to be able to bend and deform. You may want to disable LOD generation in the Import dock or tweak the generation settings when importing meshes that you plan to use with [SoftBody3D].
```

This note is _excessively_ verbose, but I don't currently have suggestions on content. 
However, I must point out that the reason why this is even a note is only ever mentioned at the end (`You may want to disable [...]`), which is really nasty. By switching the sentences around, readers that are not interested can skip ahead the huge explanation.
```suggestion
		[b]Note:[/b] You may want to disable LOD generation in the Import dock or tweak the generation settings when importing meshes that you plan to use with [SoftBody3D]. [SoftBody3D] will honor [url=$DOCS_URL/tutorials/3d/mesh_lod.html#doc-mesh-lod]mesh LODs[/url] when rendering the mesh. The physics simulation will be performed with the full level of detail, but the rendered mesh may be shown at a reduced level of detail. By default, Godot automatically generates LODs when importing meshes, and its default settings will merge adjacent faces that are nearly flat in relation to each other. This is desirable for static meshes, but often not what you want for soft bodies, if you want these faces to be able to bend and deform.
```
